name: Spell Checker
summary: A basic text-processing tool that identifies and corrects spelling errors in user-provided input without persistence or autonomous behavior.

primary_interpretation.driver: Simple pattern matching and correction within a narrow domain
primary_interpretation.constraint: No persistence, no autonomy, and no external action capability

agii.evidence: Spell checkers operate only on provided text and do not initiate, continue, or revisit tasks independently.
agii.interpretation: There is no persistent agency pressure; all activity is strictly reactive and bounded to the current input.
agii.implication: AGII is near zero, serving as a baseline for non-agentic systems.

casx.evidence: The system affects only text output within an editing environment and requires direct user interaction.
casx.interpretation: Its ability to affect the world is minimal and localized.
casx.implication: CASX is low, reflecting limited real-world impact.

trajectory.evidence: Spell checking technology is mature and shows incremental rather than transformative improvement.
trajectory.interpretation: There is little expectation of major increases in capability or autonomy.

change_levers.increase_risk: Integration into autonomous writing or communication systems with broader action capabilities
change_levers.decrease_risk: Maintaining strict input-bound operation with no external system access

classification_notes.inevitable_under_normal_use: No — impact is minimal and tightly bounded

main_uncertainty: Minimal; behavior and limitations are well understood
